label: Introduction
title: Tell Me Who Your Friends Are
epigraph: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.

body.text: Who are your friends? Tell me who your friends are, and I will tell you who you are. That is not merely a proverb of men. It is the plain testimony of Scripture, and it is the reason this book exists.

There is a law at work in the kingdom of God, and it is as dependable as the law of sowing and reaping. I call it the law of association. It says this: what a man carries, he transfers. Walk with the wise, and wisdom rubs off on you. Walk with a fool, and destruction rubs off on you. You come under blessing or under curse depending on who you keep close.

Most believers have never examined their friendships in that light. We choose our company by convenience. We choose it by tribe, by office, by who laughs at our jokes, by who is available on a Saturday. Then we wonder why our lives are stuck in one place while we pray so hard.

Let me say it plainly. Your prayer life is not your only problem. Some of us are praying for open doors while sitting daily in the counsel of people who close doors. You cannot keep drinking from a poisoned well and then blame the thirst.

This book will take you through the Scriptures and show you the law of association at work in the lives of ordinary and extraordinary people. Lot was blessed because he walked with Abraham. David's distressed, indebted and discontented men became mighty men because they attached themselves to a man of grace. Potiphar's house prospered because Joseph slept under his roof. Laban openly confessed that his increase came for Jacob's sake. A widow in Zarephath ate for many days because she obeyed a prophet. Noah's household was saved on the strength of one man's grace.

We will look at the other side too, because it is real. Solomon began well and finished badly, and the reason was the company he loved. Rehoboam inherited a divided kingdom because of a father's disobedience. There are people whose lives are a truckload of disaster, and if you stay near them long enough the same pattern will begin to show in yours.

I write as a pastor, not as a theorist. I have watched people whose lives were in a mess come into a house of God, stay, receive a turnaround, and then rise up to speak evil of the very place where God repaired them. I have watched God bless an office because one believer was posted there. These are not stories. This is the law at work.

So read this book with a pen. At the end of every chapter you will find steps to take, not merely thoughts to admire. And you will find a prayer, because everything we understand must finally be prayed.

My assignment in these pages is simple. I want you to become a carrier — a person whose presence makes families, offices, churches and nations better — and I want you to stop losing the grace God keeps sending your way because you did not recognize it.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Father, as I read this book, open my eyes to see the people You have sent to bless me, and give me courage to leave the company that is costing me my future. Make me a carrier of Your blessing, in Jesus name.

label: Chapter One
title: Who Are Your Friends?
epigraph: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.

body.text: You come under curse or under blessing depending on who you associate with. That single sentence, if you receive it, will reorder your life.

We like to believe we are strong enough to keep close company with anything and remain unaffected. Paul says do not be deceived. The word he uses for communications is not only speech; it is fellowship, exchange, the daily traffic of two lives. What is exchanged in that traffic either corrupts or builds. Nobody stays neutral.

Look at how the Bible frames it in Proverbs. It does not say the companion of fools will make a mistake. It says he shall be destroyed. That is the language of collapse, of a life pulled down. Meanwhile the one who walks with wise men shall be wise — not shall learn wisdom, shall become wise. Wisdom becomes his nature by proximity.
“And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses.”

Joshua did not attend a school of wisdom. Joshua carried Moses' bag. He stood at the door of the tent when the cloud came down. He was the young man who did not leave when everybody else went back to the camp. Years of nearness produced a man full of the spirit of wisdom, and a whole nation followed him.
Now hear the reverse in the same Scriptures.
“For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father.”
The wisest man who ever lived lost his heart by association. Not by ignorance. Not by a lack of anointing. By company he loved and would not release.

So let us be practical, because this is where the teaching earns its keep. Take the four or five people you speak with most often in a week. Not acquaintances — the ones with access to your ear. Ask of each one: what is this person transferring to me?

Some transfer courage. You leave their presence able to believe God again. Some transfer complaints. You arrive with faith and leave with a list of everything wrong with your church, your country and your marriage. Some transfer diligence, and you find yourself working better. Some transfer suspicion, and you find yourself examining people you used to trust.

You are not being unkind by noticing this. You are being a steward. Your ear is not a public road. Not everyone deserves a place at the table of your life, and there is no verse that requires you to give the seat of counsel to a person whose life is a warning.

Understand the difference between ministry and association. You may minister to a fool. You must not walk with him. Jesus ate with sinners; He built with twelve. He was called a friend of publicans; He took Peter, James and John up the mountain. Reach everybody. Walk with the wise.

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: Write the names of the five people who have the most access to your ear.
Beside each name write one word for what they transfer to you: faith, fear, diligence, gossip, courage, complaint.
Choose one name to move from the seat of counsel to the circle of ministry. Do it quietly, without a speech.
Identify one wise person you have been too proud or too shy to draw near to, and take one step toward them this week.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Lord, I will not be deceived. Show me what is being transferred into my life through the company I keep. Give me the humility to draw near to wisdom and the courage to step back from destruction, in Jesus mighty name.

label: Chapter Two
title: Same Church, Different Spirits
epigraph: Children from the same father and mother can be of different spirits.
tagline: A hard word for the household of faith

body.text: Yes, he is your brother in the Lord. Yes, she is your sister in the Lord. But do you know what spirit they are of?

This is the question the modern church does not like. We have been taught to assume every person in the building is identical in heart because we all sang the same song. But Scripture never asks us to be blind. It asks us to be discerning.

I know by experience that in every church there are people who come to build the church and people who come to pull the church down. Both groups attend. Both groups can quote Scripture. Both may be on a rota. One is building; the other is dismantling, sometimes without even knowing whose errand it is running.

I know also that there are people whose destination is settled in hell but who are in church making disciples for hell. While you are pulling the lost out of the pit, they are pushing them further down into it. You are recruiting for heaven; they are recruiting for another place. Two harvests are happening in one building.
How do you know them? Do not look for horns. Look for fruit. Their fruits expose them.

They are the ones who gossip. They are full of hatred and they are rebellious. Watch the person who cannot submit to any authority anywhere — not at home, not at work, not in the house of God. Watch the one who brings you information you did not ask for about people you were at peace with. Watch the one who is always wounded by leadership and never wounded by sin.

You cannot serve God acceptably while harbouring the articles of Satan. Gossip is an article of Satan. Hatred is an article of Satan. Rebellion is an article of Satan. A man may carry a Bible in one hand and Satan's toolbox in the other, and heaven is not confused by the arrangement.

Heaven will be full of surprises when Jesus tells people we respect, I do not know you. Let that sentence sit on you for a moment. The people we quote. The people with the platforms. The people whose voices we recognize.
“Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.”

Notice the progression David describes. First you walk with them. Then you stand with them. Then you sit down among the scornful and you are settled. Nobody joins the seat of the scornful on the first day. It begins as a walk. It begins as a conversation you should have ended.

So ask yourself the questions of Psalm 1. Who are you walking with? Who are you standing with? Who are you sitting with? And who are you listening to — because in our generation much of the counsel we absorb comes from voices we have never met, through a screen we hold in our hands at midnight.
Now let me say something that will offend, and then I will explain it. There are prophetesses who have leprosy.

Is Miriam your best friend? She led the women in praise at the Red Sea with a timbrel in her hand. That was a genuine anointing on a genuine day. But she was also part of the first gang that rose against Moses, her own brother, and she came out of that tent white with leprosy.

Here is the lesson. Because you sang with Miriam does not mean you must follow her into the gossip. The gift on a person's life is not a certificate of character. A woman may usher you into the presence of God on Sunday and into a conversation of bitterness on Monday, and you must know which invitation to accept.

Is that talkative radio your best friend? Every congregation has one — the person who receives all information and broadcasts all of it. Nothing you say in confidence survives the week. Ask yourself honestly: who is my best friend, and what is that friendship costing my walk with God?
You and I are here to depopulate hell and repopulate heaven, God helping us in Jesus name. That assignment is too heavy to carry with a crowd that is pulling in the opposite direction.

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: This week, refuse to receive one piece of gossip. Say plainly: I would rather not hear this.
Examine fruit, not gifts. Ask your closest church friends: is this person submitted to anyone?
Audit the voices you listen to at night. Remove one that leaves you cynical about the house of God.
Ask God to show you one person in your congregation who is building, and move closer to them.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Father, give me the spirit of discernment in Your own house. Let me not be deceived by gifts where there is no fruit. Deliver me from the seat of the scornful, and keep my mouth clean of gossip, in Jesus name.

label: Chapter Three
title: The Grace That Rubs Off
epigraph: And every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves unto him.

body.text: When we align with good and godly people under the Abrahamic covenant, the blessing upon them rubs off on us. That is not a theory; it is the recorded history of God's dealings with men.

Consider David in the cave of Adullam. He was not yet king. He had no palace, no throne, no treasury. And the Bible tells us who gathered to him: the distressed, the indebted, the discontented. I call them David's 3D men. Nothing was working for them. The odds were against them. If you had met them at Adullam you would not have written their names down for anything.
But they were wise in one thing, and that one thing changed everything. They identified a man of grace, and they followed him.
Read what became of these same men a chapter or two later. The grace on David rubbed off on them and they became mighty men.

One man killed eight hundred men with a spear. Another fought until his sword clave to his hand — his hand and the weapon became one from the labour of battle. They became rank keepers, men who did not break formation. They could break through a garrison of Philistines simply to bring their captain water from the well of Bethlehem, because he mentioned that he was thirsty.

Look at them. Debtors became warriors. Distressed men became men of exploit. Discontented men became loyal unto death. Nobody prophesied that over them at Adullam. Association did it. Because they were committed, David's grace rubbed off on them.
So let me ask you directly. Are you discouraged? Are you in debt? Are you discontented? Then hear this: there is a grace you must identify and submit to.

“And the LORD was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian. And his master saw that the LORD was with him, and that the LORD made all that he did to prosper in his hand.”

God blessed the Egyptian's house because of Joseph. Potiphar was an idolater. Potiphar had no covenant. Potiphar simply had a blessed man living under his roof, and by the law of association his accounts changed. If the law works for an Egyptian officer who did not know Jehovah, how much more for a believer who deliberately positions himself near grace?
Now understand what submission to grace actually looks like, because many want the transfer without the posture.

David's men did not negotiate. They kept rank. They ran errands. They stayed in the cave through the uncomfortable season, before there was a throne to celebrate. About four hundred men gathered to him, and they stayed long enough to be renamed. Men of renown are not made in a weekend conference.

God uses men. He has always used men. He could have written the law in the sky, but He gave it through Moses. He could have parted the Jordan by Himself, but He waited for the feet of priests to touch the water. If you despise the vessel, you will miss the content.

So be careful. That man of God you are criticizing or gossiping about may be the very one carrying the grace to bring you out of your circumstances. I have seen it happen more than once: the person a man mocks in June is the person whose word he needs in December.

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: Name your Adullam. Where has God placed you in this season, uncomfortable as it is?
Identify one person near you who visibly carries grace in an area where you are struggling.
Serve them in one concrete, unglamorous way this month, expecting nothing in return.
Stop one criticism. If you have spoken against a man of grace, repent of it today and, where wise, apologize.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Lord, I ask for the wisdom of David's men — to recognize grace, to submit to it, and to stay long enough to be changed by it. Turn my distress into strength and my debt into testimony, in Jesus mighty name.

label: Chapter Four
title: Identify Grace, Then Submit to It
epigraph: God will never bring people your way for nothing.
tagline: A working principle of the law of association

body.text: God always has a reason for bringing someone your way. Take time to find out why you are in a relationship with each person in your life. He brings people your way to be a blessing to you, and for you to be a blessing to them. Nothing in the kingdom is accidental.
That is why carelessness with people is so expensive. A man can dismiss in one careless month the very relationship God prepared for him over ten years.

I have seen people in church whose lives were in a mess. They came in broken. They stayed. Things changed. And then they left the church, and began to talk evil about the church and about the pastor. When I see them, their lives are pathetic again. The turnaround had not finished its work in them and they ran off.

Hear me carefully, because this is not a call to blind loyalty. Not every church is for you. Your blessing is not in every church. There is a church ordained for every person. What I am against is not moving; it is running off, and then poisoning the well you drank from.

David's men stayed for a long period until they became mighty men, men of renown. Length of stay is part of the transfer. When you partner with people of wisdom, your success in life is accelerated — but acceleration still needs a runway.

So learn to distinguish between three different seasons. There is a season of arrival, when you are new and everything is unfamiliar. There is a season of building, where the real work happens and nothing feels remarkable. And there is a season of release, when God genuinely sends you out — and He sends people out with a blessing on their lips, not a case in their mouth.
If you cannot leave a place blessing it, you are not being released. You are running.

Now the practical rules of this chapter. Stay away from people who do not honour God or His spiritual laws. Stay away from trouble. Stay away from troublemakers. Stay away from people without wisdom and understanding in the things of God.

And then turn the question around, because association is a two-way traffic. Are you a blessing to the people in your life? Does the heart of your pastor bless you continually, or does your name arrive in his office attached to a problem?

Do not criticize or envy those who are ahead of you — materially, financially or spiritually. Envy is not a small sin. By envy you drive away blessing and welcome curse upon yourself. The man you are envying is often the man God assigned to open your door.

“And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper. The ungodly are not so: but are like the chaff which the wind driveth away.”

Two men are described here, and the difference between them is rootedness. One is planted; the other is driven. One is by the river; the other is in the wind. Planted men bear fruit in season. Driven men move constantly and produce nothing, and they are usually the ones with the strongest opinions about everybody who stayed.
Which are you? Are you planted anywhere, under anyone, in anything? Or has your whole Christian life been a series of departures?

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: List the last three churches, jobs or mentors you left. Beside each, write whether you were released or you ran.
If you left speaking evil of a place God used to help you, go and make it right this month.
Name one person you have envied. Today, thank God out loud for their advancement.
Decide where you are planted for the next twelve months, and stop shopping.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Father, plant me by Your rivers. Deliver me from the spirit of the chaff that is driven from place to place. Show me why You have brought each person into my life, and let me not curse my blessing, in Jesus name.

label: Chapter Five
title: The Blessing of Abraham
epigraph: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.

body.text: God entered into a covenant to bless Abraham. Read the terms carefully in Genesis 12, because everything else in this book stands on them.

“Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing.”

Notice the first instruction. Before God discussed the blessing, He discussed relocation and separation. Get out from your country, from your kindred, from your father's house. The covenant began with a change of association.
Some of us are waiting for a blessing while God is waiting for a departure. There are family patterns, old friendships and inherited alliances that cannot follow you into what God has promised.

Now watch Lot. Lot was not a party to the covenant. God did not appear to Lot. God did not promise Lot a nation. Lot simply went with Abraham, and his association with a covenant man made him blessed also.

“And Lot also, which went with Abram, had flocks, and herds, and tents. And the land was not able to bear them, that they might dwell together: for their substance was great, so that they could not dwell together.”

See what happened. The two had to part ways — not because of poverty, not because of a quarrel over nothing, but because of blessing. Their substance was too great for one place. Strife arose between the herdsmen, and Abraham, being the elder and the wiser, said, let there be no strife between me and thee, for we be brethren.

May the problem you have be a good problem like the one Abraham and Lot had. May too much blessing be the reason relatives part ways with you. May poverty never be the reason we separate, in Jesus' mighty name.
And may the Lord bring a man of covenant and a man of blessing your way, to accelerate you and catapult you to where you ought to be.
Now understand how this reaches you and me, because we are not sons of Abraham by blood.

“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree: That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.”

This is the greatest association in the book. By the death of Jesus Christ, the Gentile is grafted into the covenant of a Hebrew patriarch. You did not earn it. You did not qualify for it. You came in the way Lot came in — by walking with the blessed One.
Isaac was prospered by the same covenant. He did not work for it; it came to him. Every blessing you will read about in the remaining chapters flows from this one arrangement.

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: Read Genesis 12 and 13 slowly, with your own family in mind.
Name one association God has been asking you to leave behind, and set a date.
Write Galatians 3:13-14 on a card and confess it daily for thirty days.
Where there is strife with a relative, take Abraham's posture first: propose peace before you defend your rights.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Lord, bring a covenant man across my path, and make me a covenant man for somebody else. Let the blessing of Abraham rest on my house through Jesus Christ, and let my parting from others be for increase and never for poverty, in Jesus mighty name.

label: Chapter Six
title: Isaac: Mightier Than a Nation
epigraph: We saw certainly that the LORD was with thee.

body.text: Isaac the son of Abraham became so blessed that an entire nation envied him, and then an entire nation came to make peace with him.

“Then Isaac sowed in that land, and received in the same year a hundredfold: and the LORD blessed him. And the man waxed great, and went forward, and grew until he became very great: For he had possession of flocks, and possession of herds, and great store of servants: and the Philistines envied him.”

Read the sequence: he waxed great, he went forward, he grew, he became very great. This is not one lucky harvest. This is a compound increase on a man who did not build the covenant he was standing on.

Then comes something remarkable. Abimelech the king sought to enter a treaty with a man. Nations enter treaties with nations. But in Isaac's case, he had become an entity. He was equated with a nation, and Abimelech saw correctly, for Isaac would become the father of nations.

“And they said, We saw certainly that the LORD was with thee: and we said, Let there be now an oath betwixt us, even betwixt us and thee, and let us make a covenant with thee … thou art now the blessed of the LORD.”

Abimelech was wise in seeking peace with a man who had become a nation. The Philistines had a choice: keep envying a blessed man, or align with him. Envy had produced nothing for them. They counselled themselves, stopped the jealousy, and took concrete steps.

Someone reading this needs to take concrete steps and stop envying others. When you rejoice with those who rejoice, your own blessings come faster. This covenant is for every Gentile, but we activate it by a right attitude. Jealousy and envy take you backwards.
How does a man become mightier than a nation? The Lord must certainly be with that man. He must be the blessed of the Lord. There is no other explanation available.

“That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies.”

Let this covenant, written now in the blood of Jesus, speak for you against every enemy until you possess their gates. May nations seek your counsel. May kings depend on your judgement. May they seek your friendship and your alliance, in Jesus name.
And in these days of unprecedented transfer of wealth, may those who truly serve God serve Him with substance.
“For God giveth to a man that is good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good before God.”

Note what the treaty required of Isaac: that he would do the Philistines no hurt. A blessed man is not a threat to his neighbours; he is a guarantee of peace. If your increase makes everyone around you poorer, examine the source of your increase.

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: Name one person whose progress has irritated you, and send them a genuine word of congratulation.
Sow something this week where you want a hundredfold, however small the seed.
Make peace with someone who has been treating you as competition.
Ask yourself: is my increase making my neighbours safer or poorer? Adjust accordingly.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Lord, deliver me from envy and make me a man of peace. Bless me and multiply me until my presence is a covenant of good to my neighbours, and let my seed possess the gates of their enemies, in Jesus mighty name.

label: Chapter Seven
title: Jacob and Laban: Blessed for Your Sake
epigraph: I have learned by experience that the LORD hath blessed me for thy sake.

body.text: Jacob fled home to his uncle Laban with nothing but a staff. He arrived as a refugee in a foreign land — and the blessing of the covenant located him there.

That is worth sitting with. The covenant is not tied to your address. When his father Isaac died, the blessing did not end. When he crossed a border, the blessing crossed with him. You will prosper where you are, because the hand of Jehovah is upon you.
“And Laban said unto him, I pray thee, if I have found favour in thine eyes, tarry: for I have learned by experience that the LORD hath blessed me for thy sake.”

Laban was not a righteous man. He was a manipulator who changed Jacob's wages ten times. But even a manipulator can read a balance sheet. He said in effect: I have run the numbers, and my prosperity started when this young man arrived.
So Laban begged him to stay. Understand what that means. The employer pleaded with the employee. The uncle pleaded with the nephew. That is what happens when a blessed man works in a man's house.
“For it was little which thou hadst before I came, and it is now increased unto a multitude; and the LORD hath blessed thee since my coming: and now when shall I provide for mine own house also?”
Jacob knew he was blessed. He did not deny it. He did not wish it or hope for it. He knew it and he said it plainly to the man's face.

Are you still struggling with poverty in your mind? Jesus became poor so that we, through His poverty, might become rich. We are children of Abraham, and children of a Father to whom the silver and the gold belong, to whom the cattle on a thousand hills belong. We are the children of a rich Father. Speak like it.

There is also a warning hidden in Laban's confession. Laban valued Jacob for what Jacob produced, not for who Jacob was. That is a common arrangement. Some people will keep you close only as long as you are useful, and will change your wages ten times while calling you family.

Jacob's response is instructive: he stayed long enough to be enriched, and then he obeyed God and left. He did not stay forever out of sentiment, and he did not leave in a rage. When God said return, he returned.

Now let me pray this over your work and your worship. May you be the reason for the blessing of God upon that company, that office, that church. May they feel your absence. May the position you leave be difficult to fill. May the office or church consult you and seek your advice even after you have gone. I pray that no church and no organization ever prays for you to leave. May you be missed in every place you have worked and every church you have attended, in Jesus name.

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: Ask honestly: has anything measurably improved in my workplace since I arrived?
Choose one thing this month to improve where you work, whether or not anyone notices.
Stop apologizing for the blessing of God on your life. Say it plainly, without boasting.
If God has said go, prepare to go with honour — no rage, no case, no bitterness.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Father, let it be said of my workplace and my church that they were blessed for my sake. Make my presence profitable and my absence felt, and when it is time to go, let me leave with honour, in Jesus name.

label: Chapter Eight
title: Esau and Ishmael: Blessed by Proximity

body.text: Coming to Esau, the twin brother of Jacob, one is tempted to think that since he was cheated out of his blessing and received nothing from Isaac his father, he was going to live a life of penury and hardship. That was not the case at all.
By reason of association with a blessed father, Esau became blessed. The same is true of Ishmael the son of Hagar. Ishmael was sent away from the household, yet he went on to become twelve tribes.
“And the angel of the LORD said unto her, I will multiply thy seed exceedingly, that it shall not be numbered for multitude.”

Think about what this means for the overflow of covenant. Neither Esau nor Ishmael was the child of promise. Neither one received the patriarchal blessing. Yet the covenant on the household was so heavy that it spilled onto the sons who were not chosen.
That is the generosity of God. When He blesses a man, the blessing exceeds the man's own portion and reaches those merely standing nearby.
Now come with me to the reunion in Genesis 32 and 33, because there is a lesson there about the size of what proximity produced.

Jacob, afraid of his brother after many years, prepared a gift. Count it: two hundred she goats, twenty he goats, two hundred ewes, twenty rams, thirty camels, forty cows, ten bulls, twenty she asses and ten colts. That is not a token. That is a caravan.

“And he said, What meanest thou by all this drove which I met? And he said, These are to find grace in the sight of my lord. And Esau said, I have enough, my brother; keep that thou hast unto thyself.”
Esau looked at a caravan of livestock and said, I have enough. The man who supposedly lost everything had so much that a fortune arriving at his gate did not move him.

May that be your testimony. May scarcity, lack and insufficiency be far from you. May our God, who does exceedingly abundantly above all we ask or think, smile upon you. May you receive the fullness of what Jesus did on the cross of Calvary, in Jesus name.

Let us gather the thread of these chapters. Jacob was blessed by association with Isaac, who was blessed because of Abraham's covenant. Ishmael and Esau were blessed for Abraham's sake. And you and I today are blessed for that same sake.
“And the LORD appeared unto him the same night, and said, I am the God of Abraham thy father: fear not, for I am with thee, and will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham's sake.”
For my servant Abraham's sake. Four words that carry generations. Now hear the same promise handed down again, to a fleeing young man sleeping on a stone.

“And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.”

Through Jesus, we are today part of this covenant of blessing. When you associate with a blessed person, you become blessed. And when you associate with the Blessed One, you become a carrier yourself.

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: Stop rehearsing what you were cheated out of. Write it down once, then hand it to God.
Name the household God has placed you near, and honour it deliberately this week.
Practise the words “I have enough” over what you already have.
Bless one person who is not obliged to bless you back.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Father, let the overflow of Your covenant reach every person standing near me — my children, my household, my staff, my neighbours. Bring me to the day when I can say, I have enough, in Jesus name.

label: Chapter Nine
title: Joseph: A Blessing at Home First
epigraph: And the LORD blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake.

body.text: The Lord was with Joseph and he was a prosperous man in the house of Potiphar. Read that again: prosperous, while a slave. The blessing does not wait for your circumstances to become respectable.

“And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that the LORD blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake; and the blessing of the LORD was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.”

Potiphar handed everything over and stopped counting. The Bible says he knew not though he had, save the bread which he did eat. A man who employs a blessed servant can stop worrying about his own accounts.

I pray for you today, that you will be the reason others are blessed. I pray that strangers and foreigners will prosper by associating with you. May the house of our masters prosper because we work there. May men receive direction by associating with you.
Then Joseph was falsely accused and thrown into prison — and the law of association followed him into the cell.
“The keeper of the prison looked not to any thing that was under his hand; because the LORD was with him, and that which he did, the LORD made it to prosper.”
From being a blessing to one family in Potiphar's house, Joseph graduated to being a blessing to a prison full of forgotten men. Eventually he became a blessing to the whole nation of Egypt.

Notice the order, because we get this backwards. Practice being a blessing at home first. Do not be a blessing outside when those at home have not known your blessing. And if you have not been a blessing to those outside your family, you are not likely to become a national blessing.

Favour before Potiphar, plus favour in prison, equals favour before Pharaoh. Joseph solved problems in a house; then he solved problems in a prison; then he was ready to solve the problems of a nation.
Pharaoh, like Abimelech, learned that associating with a blessed man is critical. He learned that walking with the wise makes you wise, and that blessed people must be kept close by.
“And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is? … Thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled.”
Genesis 41:38, 40, KJV

Joseph interpreted a dream and received instant promotion. He was already over Potiphar's house, so it was safe for Pharaoh to say, thou shalt be over my house. Promotion is rarely a leap; it is usually a recognition of what a man has already been carrying.
May you experience a sudden turnaround for good because of the problems you have solved. May the people you have blessed never forget you, in Jesus name.

Now lift your eyes higher. Many nations today are at a loss over the challenges they face. They are as lost as Pharaoh was, and their wise men have no answer. Nations all over the world need Josephs — people in whom the Spirit of the Most High dwells. Nations need men who are solutions and not problems.
It is time for the Josephs in the nations to arise. You and I carry a blessing for nations. We are called to the nations, and the nations are waiting for us.
“And all countries came into Egypt to Joseph for to buy corn; because that the famine was so sore in all lands”
There is a famine of the word in the nations. I believe nations will come in search of spiritual bread as well as physical bread to Africa. God has raised Josephs in Africa to serve the world bread.
So ask the honest question of this chapter. Is your presence a blessing? Can your absence be felt? Have people been saying that their lives have changed since they met you?

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: Start at home. Name one member of your household who has not felt your blessing lately, and act this week.
Become a solution where you are: identify one recurring problem at work and fix it quietly.
Serve faithfully in the place that feels like a prison. That is where your Pharaoh interview is being prepared.
Write down the nation or people group God keeps putting on your heart, and begin praying for it daily.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Lord, make me a Joseph in my generation. Bless the house where I serve for my sake. Find me worthy to solve the problems of my nation, and let those I have blessed not forget me, in Jesus name.

label: Chapter Ten
title: Two Women Who Recognized a Carrier
epigraph: “And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days.”

body.text: Two women in the Old Testament show us that the law of association is not only for kings and patriarchs. It works for a widow with one meal left, and for a barren woman with a spare room.

The widow of Zarephath was down to a handful of meal and a little oil. A stranger arrived and asked for the last of it. She could have shunned prophet Elijah. She could have disbelieved him or disobeyed him — and no reasonable person would have blamed her. She chose to obey.
And she, and he, and her house, did eat many days. Not one day. Many days. Association with a carrier turned her last meal into a season of provision.
We all need friends. But more than friends, we need blessed people around us.
Then there is the Shunammite woman, and her story is even more deliberate.

She perceived that Elisha was a man of God, a carrier of blessing, and she was not going to let him pass by her house again. So she built him a guest room. She furnished it — a bed, a table, a stool, a candlestick. She invested in proximity.

Count what came back to her. She who was barren gave birth to a son. When that son later died, the prophet brought him back to life. By reason of association she received privileged information about a coming famine, and she relocated in time. And when she returned after seven years, the king restored all her land to her.

“And when the king asked the woman, she told him. So the king appointed unto her a certain officer, saying, Restore all that was hers, and all the fruits of the field since the day that she left the land, even until now.”

She did not just get her land back. Every harvest that would have been hers during the seven years she was away was restored as well. God is not merely restoring your years; He is giving you all that should have been yours in those years.
The law of association carries powerful blessings with it.
Look at what both women had in common, because it is not wealth and it is not status.
Both perceived. Both acted. Both gave something before they received anything — a widow gave her last meal, a wealthy woman gave a room. And both received far beyond the size of what they gave.

How many carriers have passed through your life and left without your recognizing them? A visiting minister you never greeted. A mentor you were too busy for. A pastor you criticized. Perception is a spiritual discipline, and it costs something to act on it.

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: Ask God to show you a carrier already in your life whom you have been overlooking.
Build your version of the guest room: make a concrete, costly investment in that relationship.
Obey one instruction from God that requires your last handful of meal.
Write down what you believe God owes no man but has promised you, and ask Him for full restoration.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Father, give me the eyes of the Shunammite woman to recognize what You are sending my way, and the obedience of the widow to act on it. Restore my years and the fruit of my years, in Jesus mighty name.

label: Chapter Eleven
title: Noah: The Household That Was Saved
epigraph: “But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.”

body.text: Here is the most sobering case of association in the Bible, and it is easy to read past it.

Noah's sons, their wives and their mother were all saved from the flood. But read the text carefully: it was Noah who found grace in the sight of the Lord. His wife did not find grace. His sons did not find grace. Their wives did not find grace. One man found grace, and eight people boarded the ark.
Everything that lived outside that boat died. And the difference between life and death, for seven of the eight, was association.
Now bring that home, because this is not a flood story. It is a family story.

God's plan in saving you is that through you, salvation should reach your whole family. You are not the end of the mercy; you are the door for it. Some of us are the first believer in a bloodline, and heaven has been waiting for one man or one woman to find grace so that a household can be brought in.
So intercede accordingly. May no one in your family die a sinner, in Jesus name. May God bring salvation to your family because of you.
The families of the earth are blessed through Abraham. May families and nations be blessed because of you.

But notice also that Noah's household had to get in. Grace was on Noah; entry was still a decision for each of them. Association does not override the will. Your children will be surrounded by the grace on your life, and they will still have to walk through the door.
So build the ark and keep calling the family. Pray for them by name. Do not grow weary because the rain has not started; Noah preached for decades before a cloud appeared.

Let this be the cry of your heart: Lord, make me such a carrier of Your blessing that families, cities and nations become blessed the moment I step there. Lord, make me such a blessing that the spiritual atmosphere of nations responds to my presence.

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: Write the full names of every unsaved member of your family on one page.
Pray over that page daily for the next forty days.
Invite one of them to something — a service, a meal, a conversation — without arguing doctrine.
Keep building the ark: continue in obedience even where there is no visible result yet.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Lord, let the grace You have given me be the door my whole household walks through. Let no one in my family die a sinner. Make me such a carrier that cities and nations feel the difference when I arrive, in Jesus name.

label: Chapter Twelve
title: The Flipside of the Blessing
epigraph: A man cannot give you what he does not have.
tagline: The other half of the law of association

body.text: We have spent eleven chapters on the blessing. Now we must be honest about the other side. What happens when you associate with a man under a curse?

Let me give you a picture from the market. If you stay all day with a cassava flour seller, at the end of the day people will not be able to tell which of the two of you is the trader. Both of you will be covered in cassava flour. You do not have to sell anything to be marked by the goods.

The followers of a man always end up conducting themselves like the man. Watch any group long enough and you will see it: the same phrases, the same posture toward authority, the same appetites. So pick your associates very carefully.
When you associate with a man under a curse, you come under the atmosphere of the curse he carries. What you get is what he has, because a man cannot give you what he does not have.

Some people are disaster prone. Everything goes wrong around them, every time. They seem to be carrying a truckload of disaster. It is always one issue after another. The man is perpetually in trouble and has financial challenges all the time, and it does not matter that he earns good money.

Now hear me: I am not asking you to despise such a person. I am asking you to know the difference between a person you are sent to help and a person you should be living with. If you stay long enough around such a life, the same things begin to happen in yours.

And there is goodness here for anyone who wants it, because a curse is not a life sentence. Every kind of curse can be broken by repenting of disobedience and receiving forgiveness through the blood of Jesus. We can break clean from a curse and begin a new life of blessing. That is the whole point of Calvary.
Deuteronomy 28 spells out the blessing of obedience and the curse of disobedience. You will do well to read the whole chapter, slowly, with your own life in view. It is better to live in obedience.

Understand this principle clearly: it is not possible to have both curse and blessing operating in one person. It will always be one or the other. That is why a man can pray fervently, give occasionally, work hard, and still watch everything leak away. Something unrepented is holding the door open.

And note the difference between a curse and an attack. An attack comes from outside and is resisted by warfare. A curse operates by legal right, and it is answered by repentance. Many believers are fighting in prayer what they should be settling in obedience.

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: Read Deuteronomy 28 in one sitting this week.
Write down any area of settled disobedience in your life, and repent of it specifically, by name.
Identify one relationship where the atmosphere of disaster is transferring to you, and change the terms of access.
Choose to help such a person from a position of strength — ministry, not partnership.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Lord Jesus, I plead Your blood over every curse known and unknown in my life and my lineage. I repent of disobedience. Break the cycle of disaster around me, and let me walk in the blessing of obedience from today, in Jesus mighty name.

label: Chapter Thirteen
title: A Blessing Cannot Rest on a Curse
epigraph: Remove the curse first, and I will bless them.
tagline: What the Holy Spirit said to me in Lomé

body.text: I was in Lomé, Togo, some time ago. As I lifted up my voice to bless the congregation, the Holy Spirit told me to stop.
He said to me, I really want to bless these people, but I cannot put a blessing upon a curse. He said, remove the curse first and I will bless them.

So I stopped praying. I asked how many bonafide members of that church were not tithing, and how many did not tithe regularly. Half of the church came forward to break the curse over their lives. We had a glorious service after that deliverance.
I have never forgotten that instruction. A blessing cannot be placed over a curse. The order matters.
“Will a man rob God? Yet ye have robbed me. But ye say, Wherein have we robbed thee? In tithes and offerings. Ye are cursed with a curse: for ye have robbed me, even this whole nation.”

Read the promise attached to obedience in the same passage: bring all the tithes into the storehouse, and prove me now herewith, says the Lord of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven and pour you out a blessing that there shall not be room enough to receive it. And I will rebuke the devourer for your sakes.
Two things are promised there. An open heaven, and a rebuked devourer. Some believers have income but no retention, because nothing has ever rebuked the devourer over their finances.
Believers may not go out and commit crimes in society, but many live in disobedience to God's clear command in Malachi. The people are zealous for God and disobedient to Him in one specific area.

Some are prayer warriors and disobedient. Others are leaders who never miss a service, and yet you find abject poverty in their lives because of the curse of robbing God. Every obedient church member prospers. May God deliver the African church from the mentality of poverty through obedience to Malachi 3, in Jesus name.

Men rob governments. They steal from the public treasury and impoverish the rest of us. But a new wave of robbers has arisen inside the church: people who steal from the collection, who steal from God. How will such a person be blessed?

The manifestation of a curse is poverty, sickness and death. That is the devil's assignment — to steal, to kill and to destroy — and it runs its full course in a life under a curse. Believers are being afflicted with diseases that defy both prayer and medical treatment. Why do church people die so frequently in some congregations? A curse must take its course.
May God deliver us from curses known and unknown, in Jesus name.

New teachings are flying around now about tithing. Tithing may be in the Old Testament, but it is not old fashioned. The ten commandments have not changed because we are under grace. Stingy people will always love these strange doctrines, and it is sad that those of us who need God's word most are the quickest to reject it.

I see people whose total offerings year in and year out amount to less than one dollar, and they are praying for mega financial blessing. Did God not say that the measure we measure is what shall be measured back to us? Can you sow a handful of maize and expect a truckload of harvest?

I have digressed a little in this chapter, and deliberately, to establish one point: a blessing cannot be placed over a curse. If someone reading this has heard the warning about evil association but has never dealt with settled disobedience, the associations will change and the results will not.

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: Read Malachi 3:8-12 and be honest about where you stand.
If you have been irregular, decide the amount and the day, and begin this month.
Repent specifically of anything taken from the house of God, and restore it where you can.
Ask God to rebuke the devourer over your finances, and expect retention, not just income.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Father, I will not rob You. Forgive me where I have been disobedient in giving. Remove every curse that stands in the way of Your blessing over my life, open the windows of heaven, and rebuke the devourer for my sake, in Jesus mighty name.

label: Chapter Fourteen
title: Solomon: He Began Well
epigraph: “And his wives turned away his heart.”

body.text: Let us look now at the most expensive example of evil association in Scripture.

Solomon began very well. He offered a thousand sacrifices. He humbled himself before God and asked for divine wisdom instead of wealth or long life. God was so pleased that He gave him what he did not ask for as well. He began well. He did not finish well.

“But king Solomon loved many strange women … Of the nations concerning which the LORD said unto the children of Israel, Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods: Solomon clave unto these in love.”
God had already told him the outcome. This is not a case of a man who did not know. God said plainly: they will turn away your heart. Solomon read the warning and clave unto them in love anyway.

Seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines. And the Bible's verdict is devastating in its simplicity: his wives turned away his heart. When Solomon was old, his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father.

He went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites. He built a high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, on the hill before Jerusalem. He built for all his strange wives, who burnt incense and sacrificed to their gods.

Understand how far that fell. The man who built the temple of Jehovah also built shrines within sight of it. Association did that. Not ignorance, not weakness of intellect — love for the wrong company.
Now look at what it cost him in peace. Early in his reign Solomon testified of rest.
“But now the LORD my God hath given me rest on every side, so that there is neither adversary nor evil occurrent.”

Then read 1 Kings 11 and count the adversaries. The Lord stirred up Hadad the Edomite. God stirred him up another adversary, Rezon the son of Eliadah. And then Jeroboam, his own servant, lifted up his hand against the king. The man who had no adversary now had three, and the record says God Himself stirred them up.

God tore the kingdom in two and left only two tribes with Solomon's son, and even that was for the sake of His covenant with David. Mercy for a grandfather's obedience preserved what a father's disobedience had forfeited.
Here is the part that should make every parent tremble. King David fought his enemies so that his son Solomon could have peace. But Solomon left a legacy of many enemies to his own son Rehoboam.
Rehoboam performed dismally, and the kingdom was divided in his time. Solomon enjoyed the blessing of association with David; Rehoboam inherited the curse of disobedience from his father.
“Then said Hezekiah to Isaiah, Good is the word of the LORD which thou hast spoken. He said moreover, "For there shall be peace and truth in my days.”

Hezekiah had just been told that his sons would be carried to Babylon as eunuchs, and his response was relief that there would be peace in his own days. Are we as parents contented that there is peace in our time, and unconcerned that evil will come upon our children after we are gone?
As parents we must be careful what seeds we sow, because our children usually reap bountiful harvests of what we plant. What inheritance are we leaving?
And it is not too late to switch from curse to blessing. You can begin today to walk with the wise and become wise yourself, in Jesus mighty name.

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: Name the warning God has already given you that you have been loving your way around.
Write what you want your children to inherit spiritually, and name one habit that contradicts it.
Ask an older, wiser believer to hold you accountable in that one area for six months.
Finish well: decide now what you will still be doing for God at seventy.

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Lord, I do not only want to begin well, I want to finish well. Keep my heart perfect with You in my old age. Let me leave peace and not enemies to my children, and let the seeds I sow be a harvest of blessing for my house, in Jesus name.

label: Chapter Fifteen
title: Blessed by Association to Jesus
epigraph: “And they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.”

body.text: Everything in this book has been leading to one association. Every other one is a shadow of it.

Lot needed Abraham. David's men needed David. Potiphar needed Joseph. The widow needed Elijah. Noah's household needed Noah. But every one of those carriers was himself a man who needed grace. There is only one association in which the Carrier is Himself the source.
“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us … That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ.”
Look at the exchange. He took the curse so that we could take the blessing. That is the greatest transfer in the history of association, and it did not happen in a cave or a palace but on a tree.
So when we speak of coming under blessing by association, we are not speaking of a technique for finding successful friends. We are speaking of a Person.
Notice how association with Jesus works in the New Testament. It works exactly the way it worked with Joshua and Moses.

Peter and John stood before the council in Acts 4. They were unlearned and ignorant men by the reckoning of the scholars. But the council could not explain what they were seeing, and Scripture records their conclusion: they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.

Nobody said, these men have degrees. Nobody said these men are eloquent. They said, these men have been somewhere. Time spent with Jesus leaves a residue that religious people can detect and cannot counterfeit.

And He made the mechanism plain Himself: abide in Me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself except it abides in the vine, no more can you, except you abide in Me. Fruit is not produced by effort at the branch; it is produced by connection to the vine.
Let me therefore ask the most important question in this book. Are you associated with Jesus Christ?
Not with a denomination. Not with a choir. Not with a family reputation for religion. But Him.

If you are not sure, settle it today. Confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord, believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, repent of sin and ask Him to come into your life. That single association moves you out from under every curse this book has described and into the covenant of Abraham.
And if you are already His, then draw nearer. The transfer is proportional to the proximity. You cannot give what you do not have, and you cannot carry what you have not received.
You and I are here to depopulate hell and repopulate heaven, God helping us in Jesus name. Let us go and be a blessing.

body.heading: Take These Steps
items: If you have never given your life to Christ, pray the prayer below out loud today, and tell one believer.
Fix a daily time with Him and guard it like an appointment with a king.
Read one Gospel through this month, watching how He treated people.
Ask Him weekly: whom have You sent me to be a blessing to?

body.heading: A Prayer
lines: Lord Jesus, I come to You. Forgive my sin. I believe You died for me and that God raised You from the dead. Be my Lord from today. Redeem me from every curse, bring me into the blessing of Abraham, and let it be said of me that I have been with Jesus. Amen.

body.heading: A Prayer of Blessing Over You
lines: May the Lord bless you and multiply you. May you be greater and mightier than your enemies.
May He bring a man of covenant across your path to accelerate you and catapult you to where you ought to be. May the grace you need not pass you by unrecognized.
May nations seek your counsel, and may kings depend on your judgement. May the blessing of the covenant of Abraham upon your life bring you to the place where you lend to nations.
May you be the reason for the blessing of God upon that company, that office, that church. May your absence be felt and your place be difficult to fill.
May scarcity, lack and insufficiency be far from you, and may you come to the day when you say with Esau, I have enough.
May God bring salvation to your whole family because of you, and may no one in your household die a sinner.
And may it be said of you, as it was said of the disciples, that this one has been with Jesus. Amen.
